title: Squared Counterfactual-Density Effect Intervals at Equality under an Unknown Rough Design Density
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope; mathematical PASS with all citations verified, editorial findings unrepaired.

The delivered results determine the polynomial exponent of honest null expected length on the stated benchmark, while leaving a stretched-exponential gap between converse and achievability.

The projected score is constrained by the single covariate dimension and fixed smoothness regime, unresolved subpolynomial rate, and constants and thresholds that establish no useful practical precision; competent writing cannot supply those missing results.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived a legal normalized original-record converse and a total data-only nearest-neighbor honest interval on the unchanged benchmark, removing the occupancy logarithm and establishing polynomial exponent -2/5. The lower retains exp(-10 sqrt(log n)); the fixed one-dimensional/smoothness scope and impractical constants/thresholds leave the delivered work at subfield below the mandatory field floor. Math review passed and all five citations were verified, but three editorial findings remain unrepaired; F-stage and Lean formalization were not entered.
tldr: For the squared causal marginal-density effect \(\Psi(P)\), the honest expected interval length at marginal equality has exact polynomial exponent \(2/5\) on the stated benchmark class with an unknown bounded merely measurable design density, one-tenth covariate smoothness and outcome Lipschitz regularity. A legal normalized design-varying original-record mixture gives the lower bound \(10^{-13}n^{-2/5}\exp\{-10\sqrt{\log n}\}\). A total data-only nearest-neighbor interval, honest over the full class and uniformly short over every equality law, gives the upper bound \(10^{16}n^{-2/5}\) for public \(n\ge n_0\). It removes the empirical-cell occupancy logarithm. Only the converse's stretched-exponential, hence subpolynomial, loss remains unresolved in this bracket.
gap: \cite{KennedyBalakrishnanWasserman2023} identifies the failure of ordinary equality-null Wald inference. The credited known-uniform proposal supplies only a lower order \(n^{-16/29}\) and an upper order \(\{\log(\exp(1)n)/n\}^{2/5}\). Neither determines the honest-null-length exponent in the original unknown-design experiment.
fill: The theorem spine certifies the legal normalized and exactly centered original-record comparison and one empirical-mass interval. Its two sides identify the polynomial exponent. The occupancy-logarithm question remains separate from the exponent deliverable.
